w:r.w:t: PixelForge v14.0: Master Implementation Specification & PRD

PixelForge is a persistent visual memory and asset production workspace for game developers. It is designed for Godot-based games where visual consistency across hundreds of assets is difficult to maintain.

PixelForge does NOT replace the artist/developer. The developer creates the artistic direction. PixelForge remembers, organizes, analyzes, and accelerates that direction. The primary value is the accumulation of visual knowledge over the lifetime of a project, not the raw image generation.
Collect → Analyze → Curate → Create Proposals → Evaluate → Post-Process → Promote → Evolve
Do not over-engineer. Use standard relational structures with vector support.
Acts as a "relational Knowledge Graph." Uses standard tables and foreign keys. Recursive CTEs will handle lineage and tree structures.
Stores: Metadata, vector embeddings (pgvector), relationship edges, ratings, history, and asset specifications.
Never store raw image data in the database.

The root container (Name, Target Engine, Resolution, Grid Size).
A checklist of required assets for a biome/type (e.g., "Forest Terrain" requires Base, Edge, Corner, Path).
The permanent "need". (e.g., terrain.forest.grass_base). Contains Gameplay Requirements (Walkable, 16x16) and Export Requirements.
ID, specification_id, image_path, Lifecycle State (SANDBOX, CANDIDATE, CANON), Ratings, Lineage.
A cropped, semantic reference point. Contains boolean influence toggles (e.g., shape: true, palette: false).
User-grouped references. Must have a explicit purpose (e.g., INSPIRATION, NEGATIVE_AVOID, PALETTE_SOURCE).
The current visual truth for a Biome.
Append-only log of every major action (e.g., CANON_CHANGED, RULE_ACCEPTED, VERSION_GENERATED).
The system assists but never dictates.
The AI cannot delete assets, silently hide generated variants, overwrite a Canon asset, or modify the project's global "Art Bible" without explicit permission.
The system continuously monitors ratings. After sufficient data, it creates an AI_PROPOSAL (e.g.,
"Developer consistently rates assets with 'soft outlines' 5-stars. Add to Art Bible?"
). The developer must click [Accept] to apply it.
5. The Production Pipeline (From Prompt to Pixel)
DALL-E generates concepts, not game-ready tiles. The application must bridge this gap.
System pulls Canon, References, Art Bible, and Developer Intent to create an Art Brief.
Prompt Compiler converts Art Brief into a rigid AI API prompt.
Image AI (DALL-E) returns high-res, raw conceptual images.
Vision AI flags deviations from the Art Brief.
Pixel Quantization (apply nearest-neighbor scaling to enforce pixel-art style).
Palette Mapping (snap colors to project-approved hex codes).
Alpha Cleanup (remove anti-aliased semi-transparent pixels on edges).
User evaluates the processed, engine-ready result.
The frontend must avoid generic CRUD interfaces. Implement these specific layouts:
Displays overall completion % based on ASSET_FAMILY_TEMPLATES.
Lists warnings ("⚠ Missing Grass-to-Dirt transition in Forest Biome").
The current CANON image on top. SANDBOX variants grid below. Button: [Explore Variation].
Active Collections, toggleable Reference Snippets, and a live view of the compiled Art Brief.
Clustered automatically by Vision AI tags (e.g., "Warm", "Dense", "Noisy").
Displays file-system sync status. "Safe Replacement" UI showing Before/After comparisons of modified Canon assets and a list of affected Godot .tscn files.
Do not attempt to build the full Godot integration or the advanced Asset Doctor immediately. Follow this phase order strictly.
A user can create a Project, define an Asset Specification, write an Intent, hit "Create Proposal", view the generated image, rate it, and set it to Canon.
